text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- NEW GDP PUBLISHED, BUT THE METHOD IS OLD

Brazil's National Statistics Institute (IBGE) will be using the same methods to calculate economic growth, but as of 1997 its calculations will no longer be based on the economic census, last updated in 1985, but on simpler annual surveys of economic activity.
-- PESO FALLS IN MEXICO AND WORRIES MARKET
The Mexican peso yesterday fell to the lowest level against the dollar since the peso crisis in December 1994, causing the Sao Paulo stock exchange to open 0.6 percent lower.
-- MONETARY COUNCIL ALTERS FUND PORTFOLIOS
Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN) has approved changes to the rules governing investments made by pension funds to reduce risks and increase their solvency.
O GLOBO
-- STRAY BULLETS CLAIM THREE MORE VICTIMS IN RIO
Two bus passengers and a 13-year-old boy are the latest victims to be wounded by stray bullets in Rio de Janeiro.
-- STATES' DEFICIT IS HIGHEST SINCE 1983

The deficit run by Brazil's states is reaching record levels. Central Bank data shows the deficit, excluding interest rate costs, has reached 4 billion reais or 0.7 percent of gross domestic product, the highest since 1983.
-- NET LAUNCHES DIGITAL TV VIA SATELLITE
Net has launched its Sky digital satellite television system in Sao Paulo, giving viewers access to 40 new channels.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- ATTEMPTED JAILBREAK LEAVES FIVE DEAD
Four prisoners and one prison officer were killed during an attempted jailbreak and the ensuing rebellion by inmates at the Casa de Detencao jail in Sao Paulo.
-- ONE MORE BABY DIES IN BOA VISTA HOSPITAL
One more baby has died at a hospital in Boa Vista in the Amazonian state of Roraima bringing the total number of babies who have died there in recent weeks to 36.
-- SALARIES IN SAO PAULO INDUSTRY RISE 9.2 PCT
The average real salary in Sao Paulo industry has risen 9.2 percent in September, compared with September last year.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
